sources.facts: Museum publication of the surveyed four wood bastions, approximately 2,500 square metres, plan parallel to the Saint Lawrence and remains of well, guardhouse and smithy.
Parks Canada designation at 214 Place D’Youville describes relevant stone wall and metalworking remains.
McGill catalogue MSG 1332-7 describes a first-settlement sketch by Jean Bourdon naming a chapel, stores and landing. Dating and scale are uncertain.
Archives de Montréal explicitly catalogue the 1884 series VM66,S1,P005 containing the bird’s-eye view of Montréal from 1645 to 1650.
Original 1884 Morin drawing and volume are confirmed by UQAM, which identifies the view as hypothetical.
The partial bastion was discovered under a sidewalk roughly two metres below today’s ground.
